sessions.title: Post-Graduation Path Dilemma
sessions.description: Evaluating career directions immediately after graduating: Big Tech vs. Early-Stage AI Startup vs. Research Master's vs. Solo Bootstrapping.

criteria.name: Compensation & Financial Stability
criteria.description: Base salary, benefits, signing bonus, and immediate ability to build savings or pay off student loans.

criteria.name: Learning Velocity & Skill Growth
criteria.description: Pace of acquiring high-leverage technical and architectural skills under seasoned mentorship.

criteria.name: Stress & Burnout Risk
criteria.description: Expected hours, cognitive exhaustion, on-call fire drills, and mental health sustainability (lower is better).

criteria.name: Creative Autonomy & Ownership
criteria.description: Degree of freedom to propose solutions, own end-to-end features, and avoid corporate red tape.

criteria.name: Brand Prestige & Exit Options
criteria.description: Signaling power on resume, alumni network strength, and downstream opportunities for the next 5 years.

criteria.name: Downside & Career Uncertainty
criteria.description: Risk of layoffs, runway exhaustion, market failure, or financial vulnerability (lower is better).

options.name: Option A: Tier-1 Tech Company (Big Tech SWE)
options.description: Established corporate engineering role with high compensation, formal mentorship, and structured leveling.

c-comp.note: High starting TC with stock grants and 401(k) matching.

c-learn.note: Strong formal code reviews, but scoped to narrow legacy internal frameworks.

c-stress.note: Standard 40h weeks with occasional on-call shifts.

c-autonomy.note: Strict review boards and slow consensus cycles.

c-prestige.note: Gold standard brand on any engineering CV globally.

c-risk.note: Low risk outside of macro industry tech layoffs.

options.name: Option B: Seed/Series-A AI Startup
options.description: Join an 8-person team building developer tooling. High equity potential and broad responsibilities.

c-comp.note: Below-market cash salary offset by illiquid option grants.

c-learn.note: Forced to learn infrastructure, frontend, product, and ops simultaneously.

c-autonomy.note: Direct access to founders, direct push to production.

c-prestige.note: Recognized within early-stage tech circles, less known by general recruiters.

c-risk.note: 18 months runway; survival hinges on product-market fit.

options.name: Option C: Research Master's / PhD
options.description: Two-year specialized graduate degree focused on Machine Learning and Distributed Systems.

c-comp.note: Modest research stipend ($28k/yr) and student budget.

c-learn.note: Deep theoretical foundation, though less day-to-day production DevOps experience.

c-stress.note: Flexible schedule, but paper submission deadlines create acute crunch periods.

c-autonomy.note: Select own research topics and exploratory lab experiments.

c-prestige.note: Advanced degree required for specialized research and R&D lab roles.

c-risk.note: Opportunity cost of 2 years out of the industry job market.

options.name: Option D: Indie Hacking & Freelance Consulting
options.description: Bootstrapping niche SaaS products while taking part-time client contracts to pay the bills.

c-comp.note: Lumpy client income; subscription revenue takes months or years to compound.

c-learn.note: Learn full-stack engineering, copywriting, customer support, and sales.

c-stress.note: Blurry work-life boundaries and continuous revenue anxiety.

c-autonomy.note: 100% ownership over hours, tech stack, and roadmap.

c-prestige.note: Respected by founders; corporate HR often questions the gap.

c-risk.note: Zero safety net; failure rate on solo SaaS exceeds 90%.
